root_cause: No execution grounding: drafts that return 0 rows (literal/format/join-direction errors) are shipped unverified, and vague 'which X' questions get narrow projections
what: Add an execute-and-repair loop: run the draft SQL read-only, and if it errors or returns zero rows spend the second policy call on a repair prompt containing the error/empty-result plus targeted probes (actual stored literals via LIKE tokens, candidate filter-column value samples, FK join keys) so the model can fix case/spacing/wrong-column/negation mistakes. Also add explicit output-shape rules (bare 'which/show X' -> SELECT *, keep duplicates unless asked otherwise, no extra columns) to fix projection-width misses.

root_cause: Single-shot generation never validates literals against DB contents, so unverified string predicates silently yield 0 rows
what: solve.py now executes the draft query and, only if it errors or returns zero rows, spends the second policy call on a repair turn containing the error/empty-result signal, column descriptions and sampled real values of the columns used in the filters. system_prompt.md gains value-matching rules (partial/case-insensitive matching, verify literals) and Spider projection conventions ('details'/unqualified entity questions -> all columns of the main table).
decision: s2 achieves the highest evolve score (93.33 vs 90.0 for s1 and 83.33 incumbent) with zero broken tasks, fixes a strict superset of s1's repairs (adds sp0894), and does so at lower token cost (1167 vs 1403) with fewer files; its execution-grounded literal-verification repair is a general mechanism rather than task-specific patching.

root_cause: Result-shape mismatch on executable queries: join fan-out duplicates rows where gold dedups, and 'which entities' questions need all joined tables' columns rather than T1.*
what: system_prompt.md now tells the model to default to SELECT DISTINCT for entity/name listings over joins (unless counts/aggregates or explicit duplicates), and to use bare SELECT * across all joined tables when the question asks which entities qualify or asks for details, replacing the narrower T1.* rule that caused sp0755.

root_cause: Join fan-out duplicates entity rows: listing questions over 1-to-many/link tables ship non-DISTINCT drafts, and the repair loop only triggers on errors/empty results so extra rows are never caught
what: Add a duplicate-row signal to the execute-and-repair loop: when a draft has no GROUP BY/aggregation/DISTINCT but returns repeated identical rows (typical join fan-out), spend the second policy call on a targeted rewrite prompt asking for DISTINCT without changing filters/columns. Also tighten the system prompt's DISTINCT rule to cover plain entity-listing joins (sp0536). This targets row-multiplicity failures rather than the literal-matching pattern P1 already fixed.

root_cause: Join fan-out duplicates entity rows on listing questions: the execute-and-repair loop only fires on errors/zero rows, so a non-DISTINCT draft that repeats identical rows ships unverified
what: Add a duplicate-row signal to solve.py's repair trigger: when an executable draft has no DISTINCT/GROUP BY/aggregation and its returned rows contain exact duplicates (classic 1-to-many/link-table fan-out), spend the second policy call on a targeted rewrite prompt asking for SELECT DISTINCT of exactly the requested columns. Also make the system prompt's DISTINCT rule concrete for join-based listings. This is r1s2's diagnosis but with a narrower, evidence-backed trigger (observed duplicates in the actual result) instead of a blanket rewrite, avoiding its regressions.

root_cause: Executable-but-wrong result shape: entity listings over 1-to-many/link joins ship one row per join match instead of one row per entity, because the DISTINCT rule is conditioned on an explicit 'unique' keyword
what: Rewrite the DISTINCT bullet in system_prompt.md into an operational rule: any listing of entities/names filtered through a 1-to-many or link table must use SELECT DISTINCT (including 'everybody/all/which X are ...' phrasings), while counts/aggregates, ORDER BY+LIMIT superlatives and explicitly requested duplicates stay non-distinct. Draft-time fix, no extra policy calls.
